source_citation: Grenier et al. (2011), From the western boundary currents to the Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent: Modeled pathways and water mass evolutions, Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans 116, doi:10.1029/2011JC007477.
source_locator: Grenier et al. (2011), Introduction [5] and Figure 1 caption: NICU along eastern New Ireland and separate NGCU/SICU; section 2.1 [12]â€“[15]: 0.25-degree model and gateway limitations; section 3.2 [22] and coastal pathway discussion. Relevant text read; no source axis digitized.
source_access: Publisher relevant introduction, model description/validation and pathway discussion read; no full-article read or source geometry digitization claimed.
scope: Declared regional east-coast New Ireland reach from an OSW southeastern offshore gate near 153.6 E, 4.5 S to an OSW northern offshore gate near 150.9 E, 2.2 S. Excludes Solomon Strait inflow across the basin, New Britain and St Georges branches, Bismarck Sea westward continuation, retroflection and downstream EUC route. Gates are editorial truncations, not whole-current origin or termination.
layer: Subsurface thermocline boundary-current geography. Grenier et al. discuss density-dependent modeled pathways; no single fixed-depth axis or whole-depth current footprint extracted for this coastal reach.
source_model: ORCA025-G70, 0.25-degree eddy-permitting OGCM, 46 vertical levels; five-day mean outputs.
source_model_limitations: St Georges Channel closed by model resolution, not physically absent.
NGCU core poorly simulated at the PNG mooring; coastal position sensitivity noted.
The model source pathways are not a measured NICU centerline.

other_source_access.access: Publisher page returned internal retrieval error; no additional numeric extraction.
